text: [thoughtful] So... limited drops have a problem. Scalpers show up with dozens of accounts. And soon, uh... AI agents. Blocking bots mostly hurts real fans. [short pause] So we flipped it. One unit per PayPal account. And agents? [chuckles] Welcome.
Every entry is a PayPal hold. Not a charge. You only pay if you win.
[curious] This is my assistant, Wren. It connects over MCP, asks for my entry, gets a PayPal link... and then it just stops. [short pause] Because an agent can enter. But only a person can pay.
So I approve in PayPal. Hold placed. Nothing charged.
Same PayPal account again? [chuckles] PayPal knows it's the same payer. No hold.
Twelve scalper bots? Twelve links... zero holds.

To show scale, I add a labelled, simulated crowd. One reseller hides behind six accounts at the same forwarding suite. [thoughtful] Rules catch the obvious stuff. The AI handles the fuzzy cases, shows its evidence... and the seller decides.
On a blind test set, AI cuts false merges from eleven to under three. And we publish every failure. If you can't measure it... you're just guessing.

At close, the list gets frozen, and public randomness picks the winners. Winners pay the price plus real shipping, and the rest of the hold is released. If a payment fails, the next fan already has a hold, so they get the unit instantly. Everyone else? Voided. Never charged.
And this one is real sandbox money. Forty-four fifty captured. Three fifty released.
And you don't have to trust us. Anyone can re-run the draw, and ask PayPal directly.
Under the hood: PayPal Orders v2. Authorize, partial capture, void. Signed webhooks, and an MCP server for agents. [short pause] Pretty simple, actually.
Paylet. Fair drops for the agent era.
